issue.standard_remedy: Harmonize prices to the best plant / global agreement
issue.summary: Pays 18.7% on average above the best plant for the same materials

plan.diagnosis: Houston, TX plant pays an average premium of 18.7% above best-plant pricing for 237 materials sourced from Apex Components Inc. through Oracle EBS R12, resulting in USD 3,944,234 in excess spend over the trailing 12 months. Root cause is lack of price harmonization and absence of a global or corporate purchasing agreement that would extend best-achieved pricing across all plants.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct detailed price benchmark analysis across all plants purchasing the 237 materials from Apex Components Inc., identifying best-plant prices and Houston's specific premium line items

Initiate commercial negotiation with Apex Components Inc. to establish global pricing agreement based on best-plant rates, leveraging total company spend volume and threat of consolidation to alternate suppliers
remedy_steps.owner: Strategic Sourcing Lead with Procurement Director approval

remedy_steps.step: Execute master purchasing agreement with harmonized pricing across all plants, updating Oracle EBS R12 purchase price variances and item master records for Houston facility
Implement monthly price compliance monitoring dashboard tracking Houston plant purchases against global agreement rates, with auto-alerts for exceptions >2%
Conduct quarterly business reviews with Apex Components Inc. to ensure adherence to pricing terms and identify additional standardization opportunities across the 237 materials

plan.expected_impact: Elimination of the 18.7% price premium will generate USD 3,944,234 in annual savings once harmonized pricing is fully implemented across all 237 materials purchased by Houston plant
kpis: Price variance reduction: Target 18.7% premium to 0% within 90 days
Contract compliance rate: >98% of Houston POs at global agreement pricing
Maverick spend reduction: <2% of Houston purchases off-contract for the 237 materials
risks: Apex Components Inc. may resist global pricing harmonization, requiring escalation or competitive tender
Houston plant may have unique specifications or delivery requirements justifying partial premium (requires validation)
Implementation delays in Oracle EBS R12 price master updates could defer savings realization
Supplier capacity constraints if Houston volume was previously supporting premium pricing model
erp_actions: Oracle EBS R12: Update purchase price lists (PO_PRICE_LISTS) for all 237 materials to reflect negotiated global pricing for Houston operating unit
Oracle EBS R12: Create approved supplier list entries linking Apex Components Inc. to standardized item-plant combinations with new pricing effective date
Oracle EBS R12: Configure purchasing approval workflow to flag any Houston PO for these 237 materials exceeding global agreement price by >2%
Oracle EBS R12: Implement blanket purchase agreement (BPA) at corporate level with release hierarchy allowing Houston plant call-offs at standard rates
Cross-ERP: If same materials purchased in SAP/Dynamics/NetSuite plants, replicate pricing harmonization (SAP: INFO records update, Dynamics: Trade agreements, NetSuite: Item pricing rules)
Coupa: Create catalog punch-out or hosted catalog for the 237 Apex materials with locked global pricing to prevent maverick buying
